directAnswer: To reset PCIe storage, you typically need to access your system's BIOS/UEFI settings and perform a reset of the NVMe controller or the storage device itself.
summary: Resetting PCIe storage can help resolve issues related to performance or connectivity. The process varies slightly depending on the platform.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Steps
sections.body: The steps to reset PCIe storage can differ based on your motherboard and BIOS version. Below are general guidelines for Windows and Linux systems.

sections.heading: Caveats
sections.body: Resetting PCIe storage may lead to data loss. Ensure you have backups of important data before proceeding.

steps.title: Access BIOS/UEFI
steps.detail: Restart your computer and press the appropriate key (often F2, DEL, or ESC) to enter BIOS/UEFI settings.

steps.title: Locate PCIe Storage Settings
steps.detail: Navigate to the 'Advanced' or 'Storage' tab, and find the NVMe configuration settings. The exact path may vary by motherboard manufacturer.

steps.title: Reset NVMe Controller
steps.detail: Select the option to reset the NVMe controller or the specific PCIe storage device. Confirm your choice.

steps.title: Save and Exit
steps.detail: Save the changes and exit BIOS/UEFI. Your system will restart.

faqs.question: Will resetting my PCIe storage erase my data?
faqs.answer: Resetting the PCIe storage does not typically erase data, but it's recommended to back up important files before proceeding.

faqs.question: What if I can't find the NVMe settings in BIOS?
faqs.answer: If NVMe settings are not visible, check your motherboard manual or manufacturer's website for specific instructions.

faqs.question: Can I reset PCIe storage from the operating system?
faqs.answer: Some operating systems allow for software-based resets or troubleshooting, but accessing BIOS/UEFI is the most reliable method.

caveats: Data loss may occur if not backed up prior to resetting.
